item.title: Version 0.3.16-beta.2
item.description:
This is a beta build (0.3.16-beta.2, build 51). Switch the update channel to Stable in Settings > About to stay on production releases.

Workspaces without losing context

  • Click the repository title to search and switch between the current repository's workspaces, other open windows, pinned repositories, and recent repositories; refresh workspace state directly in the picker.
  • Workspace rows show the working-copy change, description, conflicts, age, and changed-file count. The Repository List now groups recent sibling workspaces beneath their primary repository.
  • Forget keeps the checkout on disk, while Forget & Delete closes matching windows and removes only the verified checkout after jj forgets it.

Cursor Origin and CLI settings

  • Open or create Cursor Origin pull requests with the authenticated origin CLI, including one dependent pull request per change from the stacked-PR workflow.
  • Settings now groups version-control and forge CLIs (jayjay, jj, gh, glab, and origin) in a dedicated CLI tab.

Fixes

  • Dragging the working-copy @ chip over an immutable change now gives a terse refusal and cancels quietly; dropping a change onto its only parent no longer creates a no-op rewrite.
  • Removing a conflicted bookmark from one DAG change keeps its other targets intact.
  • Deeply nested property lists fall back to the raw view instead of overflowing the parser stack, and jj-lib futures get enough stack when mutations run from macOS worker threads.
  • Workspace removal waits for repository work, handles path aliases, restores the window when forgetting fails, and cannot delete an unrelated directory that replaced the selected checkout path.

item.title: Version 0.3.16-beta.1
item.description:
This is a beta build (0.3.16-beta.1, build 50). Switch the update channel to Stable in Settings > About to stay on production releases.

Edit files and resolve conflicts in JayJay

  • Working-copy files can now be edited directly in JayJay: Edit opens a syntax-highlighted modal and saves straight into the current change.
  • Edit in JayJay resolves conflicts without leaving the app: Base-relative Left and Right sources on top, per-hunk Accept Left / Base / Right below, Option-Left/Right shortcuts, and a Raw mode for direct marker editing. Complete and partial resolutions both save, and n-way jj conflicts stay editable through their markers.

JayJay as a jj tool

  • JayJay now runs as jj's diff viewer, diff editor, and merge tool in blocking sessions; copy a paste-ready configuration from Settings > Tools or jayjay config.
  • Diff-edit sessions select individual lines, keep or discard whole binary and non-text files, and carry executable-bit changes; merge sessions reuse the in-app hunk resolver.
  • Closing a tool window cancels the session with the exit status jj expects, so an abandoned session never counts as an accepted edit.

Beta update channel

  • The new update channel dropdown in Settings > About switches between Stable and Beta; the Beta channel receives pre-release builds like this one through the regular update check.

Fixes

  • Actions that would rewrite immutable changes (edit, squash, rebase, abandon, describe) are no longer offered, and the core refuses them everywhere else.
  • An open conflict resolution now survives working-copy snapshots, and saving over a conflict that changed underneath is rejected instead of silently discarding the incoming side.
  • Repeated identical conflict blocks resolve at their own occurrence instead of the first match.
  • Image files, including SVGs, stay read-only in diff views, and renamed text files keep their Edit action.
  • The scroll wheel now reaches the surrounding list when hovering sized-to-content diff cards, and tool windows fit small displays.

item.title: Version 0.3.15
item.description:
Choose your update channel

  • A new update channel dropdown in Settings > About switches between Stable and Beta. The Beta channel receives pre-release builds through the regular update check; Stable stays on production releases only.
  • Upcoming features will ship to the Beta channel first — switch to Beta to try them early and help catch issues before they reach everyone.

item.title: Version 0.3.14
item.description:
Syntax highlighting

  • Diffs now include syntax highlighting for Kotlin, C#, and PHP source files.

Fixes

  • Opening a repository no longer hangs while JayJay enumerates workspaces when the working copy cannot be snapshotted, including repositories watched by a paused Watchman service.
  • Edit Diff is no longer offered for immutable, conflicted, or empty changes, or while comparing revisions.

item.title: Version 0.3.13
item.description:
Native GitHub pull request stacks

  • Submitting a GitHub PR stack now links its pull requests into GitHub's native stacked-PR experience, including the stack overview and merge-as-a-stack controls.
  • After submission, Done opens the top pull request for a linked GitHub stack or the highest merge request for GitLab. If GitHub native linking is unavailable, the existing dependent pull requests remain usable and JayJay opens each one.

Fixes

  • Edit Diff stays responsive while selecting or deselecting lines and scrolling, including large files with syntax-highlighted comments.
  • The running app's Dock icon now follows the system's light or dark appearance while preserving the development badge in debug builds.

Compatibility

  • Updated JayJay's embedded Jujutsu libraries to version 0.44.0.

item.title: Version 0.3.12
item.description:
Expand collapsed context

  • Collapsed "N unmodified lines" separators are now interactive: Show 10 reveals the next chunk beside the change and Show all expands the whole region, in both unified and side-by-side views.
  • Regions that fit in one chunk show a single Show all, and the links match the separator text until you hover — pointer cursor and hover underline mark them as clickable.
  • New command palette action Expand All Unmodified Lines expands every collapsed region of the visible diff from the keyboard.
  • Repeated reveals are fast on large files: syntax highlighting is computed once per file and reused, and revealed lines inside multiline constructs (like block comments) highlight correctly even when the opening marker is still hidden.
  • Expansion failures show as a small dismissible banner in the diff pane instead of a blocking alert.

Edit Diff mode for large changes

  • File cards collapse and expand individually, with per-file +/− line counts in each header and Expand All / Collapse All buttons (⌥⌘E / ⌥⌘C).
  • Large changes start collapsed automatically — over 30 files with more than 1,000 changed lines folds everything, and files over 300 changed lines fold individually — so entering Edit Diff on a big change stays instant and tidy.
  • Full keyboard flow: j/k or arrow keys move between file cards, ←/→ collapse or expand the focused card, Return toggles it, and Space selects its changed lines.
  • Select All is dramatically faster on moderate and large diffs.
  • Cards render full-height without nested scrolling, and binary property lists show their readable XML preview.

Fixes

  • Files that quote conflict markers (like documentation about <<<<<<<) no longer render conflict-styled or prevent context from collapsing.
  • Toggling Ignore Whitespace mid-action can no longer apply edits or expansions against the wrong version of a diff.
  • Scroll position stays anchored correctly when revealing context above the viewport, and in diffs with multiple conflicts.

item.title: Version 0.3.11
item.description:
Improved

  • Send Feedback is available from the Help menu and the command palette, opening a pre-addressed email.

Fixes

  • Closing the only repository window after relaunching from the Dock now returns to the Repository List instead of leaving the window stuck in an unclosable state.
  • A minimized repository window is restored by Dock reopen again instead of being replaced by the Repository List.
  • Windows restored on a changed display arrangement are kept within the visible screen.

item.title: Version 0.3.10
item.description:
Improved

  • Pull and Push actions now show directional in-flight feedback while synchronizing with a remote.

Fixes

  • Repository switching and the repository list now work reliably from restored or secondary windows, while reusing the existing main window instead of opening a duplicate.
  • Fixed the remaining commit-box draft issues when moving between working-copy changes, including stale messages on new changes and lost typed drafts.
  • A pending bookmark push is no longer lost when another push is already in progress.

item.title: Version 0.3.9
item.description:
New

  • Repositories can now be pinned from the repository list, keeping persistent projects separate from recent history.
  • The repository title now opens a menu for switching between open windows, reopening pinned repositories, returning to the repository list, or opening another repository.

Fixes

  • Review-note context can now be selected and copied across multiple lines.
  • Pinned repositories stay synchronized across running JayJay shells and remain accurate after storage resets or failed writes.

item.title: Version 0.3.8
item.description:
New

  • HTML changes can now be rendered inside JayJay in a sandboxed preview, including repository-relative styles and images, while the external-open action remains available.
  • Markdown previews now render repository-relative images, and rich previews use a compact, stable gutter.
  • The font picker recognizes a wider set of installed developer fonts.
  • The Dock icon now follows the system’s light or dark appearance.

Fixes

  • Repository windows opened from the repository list or Dock now appear at their normal size with the full toolbar immediately, without flashing a tiny intermediate window.
  • Closing the last repository returns to the repository list, and Dock menu actions now open the picker or recent repository reliably.
  • Window and diff resizing is smoother; large diffs rewrap after a live resize instead of on every resize tick.
  • Diff Edit and line-level discard now reject stale, conflicted, renamed, or immutable sources instead of rewriting unsupported or outdated content.
  • Bookmark drag targets remain available throughout the drag, and Escape closes Diff Edit.
  • The Conflicts filter now uses Jujutsu’s correct conflicts() revset.

item.title: Version 0.3.7
item.description:
New

  • Compact DAG lanes make dense change graphs easier to scan without widening the sidebar.

Fixes

  • Conflict blocks now mark each content line as base, destination, rebased, or side, so the source of each line is visible without reading the compact header.

Under the Hood

  • The bundled command-line tool is a thin launcher again, while review-note commands run through the macOS app and shared core logic.
  • Release packaging removes unused preview resources, strips release binaries, and keeps a separate dSYM archive for crash-log symbolication.

item.title: Version 0.3.6
item.description:
New

  • Rich diff previews for Markdown, notebooks, CSV/TSV tables, binary property lists, and SARIF reports.
  • Text-backed formats still open as raw diffs by default, with a preview button when a richer view is available.
  • Working-copy HTML files can open in the default app from the diff header, so linked CSS and images work normally.
  • Changed-line diffs now highlight the smallest changed text with subtler word backgrounds.

Fixes

  • Repository initialization now shows the underlying jj git init error and hint instead of a generic failure.
  • Show in Finder from the file list context menu now reveals the selected file reliably.
  • Switching rich previews no longer flashes through the processed text view.

Under the Hood

  • Diff projection, source-preview, and external-preview behavior is documented and covered by shared CSV, notebook, property list, Markdown, HTML, and SARIF fixtures.

item.title: Version 0.3.5
item.description:
New

  • Local review notes let humans and coding agents leave, edit, and resolve line-anchored comments on changed files without leaving JayJay.
  • Notes show in the diff gutter, inline diff text, file list badges, and the change review summary.
  • The jayjay review CLI command reads and writes the same local review store, so agents can exchange review context with the app.

Under the Hood

  • Review marks and notes now use a shared Rust store across SwiftUI, GPUI, and CLI surfaces, with atomic writes and corrupt-file preservation.

item.title: Version 0.3.4
item.description:
New

  • Describe button in the commit box — save the working copy’s description with jj describe without starting a new change.

Fixes

  • The split dialog now shows the files being split immediately, below the message field so the focused field no longer jumps, and long file lists scroll instead of growing the dialog.
  • Editing a commit from the context menu now loads its description into the commit box instead of keeping a stale draft — and a typed draft survives splitting files out of the working copy.
  • Abandoning lines via Edit Diff on other revisions no longer leaves the graph showing stale rows until the next refresh.

Under the Hood

  • Jujutsu library upgraded to 0.43.
  • GitHub Actions are now pinned to commit SHAs.

item.title: Version 0.3.3
item.description:
Fixes

  • Renaming a file without changing its contents no longer shows a misleading all-green diff — it now reads “No content changes.”

Under the Hood

  • Smaller download — the bundled Help screenshots now ship as optimized JPEGs.

item.title: Version 0.3.2
item.description:
Keyboard Shortcuts

  • A new keyboard-shortcut cheatsheet opens with ⌘/ (or Help › Keyboard Shortcuts) — a native, two-column reference of every shortcut, replacing the old web link.

Bookmarks

  • The Bookmark Manager now shows each tracked bookmark’s state against its remote — in sync, ahead, behind, or diverged, with the commit counts.
  • Deleted bookmarks are hidden by default and easier to clean up, and stale remote-only bookmarks are clearer to spot.

Compare & Operation Log

  • Compare two divergent versions of the same change to see which is safer to abandon (right-click a divergent change › Compare Divergent Versions).
  • The Operation Log window gained per-operation icons, a bolded change-id prefix, and sizing consistent with the rest of the app.

Status Bar

  • The status bar now surfaces working-copy edit stats, the active bookmark’s sync state, a divergent-change count, and the last operation — each with a small icon.

Fixes

  • “Pull Request” now opens the new-PR page even when the host lookup can’t complete (offline, or gh/glab missing) instead of failing right after a push.

item.title: Version 0.3.1
item.description:
Command Palette

  • Command palette polish (⇧⌘P) with fuzzy search, shortcut glyphs, and a searchable keybind cheatsheet that remembers its position between launches.
  • Switch appearance straight from the palette with Theme: System, Theme: Light, and Theme: Dark.

Log & DAG

  • Author avatars now resolve real images for GitHub bot accounts (for example dependabot[bot]) and for GitLab users, instead of falling back to a Gravatar identicon.
  • A change’s age reads in whole minutes (“1 minute ago”) rather than ticking second by second.

Fixes

  • Starting a new change no longer carries the previous change’s message into the commit box.
  • The file-column row separator now aligns with the filename instead of the checkbox.

Security

  • Hardened handling of untrusted repository content: repository-controlled filenames are passed to jj as literal paths (never as options or fileset expressions), LFS diff-hiding follows real LFS registration rather than .gitattributes alone, and oversized files no longer load fully into memory for preview.

item.title: Version 0.3.0
item.description:
Requirements

  • JayJay 0.3 requires macOS 26 or later. If you are on an earlier macOS version, consider updating to macOS 26 to get this and future releases.

Stacked Pull Requests

  • Select a linear stack of changes and submit them as dependent pull requests — one per change, with dependent bases and editable titles — on GitHub and GitLab.
  • On-device Apple Intelligence suggests kebab-case bookmark names from your change descriptions, with a progress indicator while they generate and a deterministic fallback when it is unavailable.
  • The submit step verifies the forge CLI and rejects divergent or duplicate-bookmark stacks before moving or pushing anything, and Settings show GitHub (gh) and GitLab (glab) CLI status and version.

Log & DAG

  • Change and commit IDs highlight their shortest unique prefix in bold with the remainder dimmed, so you can identify changes at a glance.
  • DAG rows show author avatars from GitHub or Gravatar next to the author name.
  • Drag a bookmark onto a change in the DAG to move it, with a “Move … here?” bubble and a highlighted drop target showing the destination before you release.

Diffs & Editing

  • The file column has a new toggle to switch between a tree and a flat list of changed files.
  • The commit box splits its message into Summary and Description fields, GitHub Desktop style, which combine into a single jj change description for clean PR titles and bodies.
  • Annotate/blame shows syntax-highlighted file content, with color-coded change IDs grouping lines by the change that introduced them.
  • Annotate and File History now use explicit Exit buttons.

Integrations

  • GitLab merge requests are supported: open them directly from bookmarks on gitlab.com remotes, including nested group namespaces, with pipeline status shown in the merge request view. Set GITLAB_TOKEN for private projects and higher rate limits.
  • Cursor joins VS Code, VSCodium, Zed, and Xcode as an external editor, opening with --classic so the editor layout appears instead of the Agent window.

item.title: Version 0.2.28
item.description:
Stability

  • JayJay now preserves the same command environment for background jj and Git operations, fixing push and remote workflows that depend on your shell PATH or SSH agent.
  • Repository refresh, bookmark diff, conflict, and restore workflows handle more jj edge cases without dropping into raw command output.

Diffs & Review

  • Diff Edit has a new bulk selection control for selecting or clearing every editable file in the view.
  • Large diffs render faster and keep wrapping, placeholders, and file navigation more stable.

Updates

  • The About settings now include anonymous usage stats as an opt-in update-check setting.
  • Release tooling and CI checks were tightened so appcast, Homebrew, and packaged app validation stay in sync.

item.title: Version 0.2.27
item.description:
Command Line

  • The jayjay launcher now opens repositories in your already-running app, and opens a fresh window even when none is showing.
  • Homebrew installs now place jayjay on your PATH automatically, kept in sync with the app.

Diffs & Conflicts

  • Errors from jj commands — such as a failed conflict resolution — now read as a plain sentence instead of raw command output.

item.title: Version 0.2.26
item.description:
Pull Requests

  • Added Codeberg pull request support alongside GitHub, so you can open and track PRs from Codeberg-hosted repositories.

Large Repositories

  • Opening a large repository (for example a multi-gigabyte Chromium checkout) no longer stalls on a working-copy snapshot — the graph appears immediately, while smaller repos still refresh eagerly on open.
  • Git submodule status is now optional and off by default, avoiding slow submodule scans on huge repositories. Enable it in Settings when you need it.

Toolbar & Interface

  • Added a spinning refresh indicator in the toolbar so it is clear when the repository is refreshing.
  • The change header now reloads its insertion and deletion counts when the working copy is amended, instead of showing stale numbers.
  • Fixed “Reveal in Finder” to fall back gracefully, and corrected the file-list header height.

item.title: Version 0.2.25
item.description:
Onboarding

  • Fixed an empty segmented tab bar that appeared at the top of the welcome screen on macOS 26. The onboarding flow now uses a clean page indicator with Back/Next navigation.
  • Onboarding and welcome windows now size correctly, accounting for the title bar height instead of coming up slightly short.

Performance

  • Abandoning working-copy lines now refreshes only the affected change and updates the working-copy row in place, instead of re-snapshotting and rebuilding the whole graph.

Core

  • Updated the Jujutsu engine to jj-lib 0.42.0.

item.title: Version 0.2.24
item.description:
Editors

  • Added VSCodium to the built-in editor list, alongside Visual Studio Code, Zed, Xcode, and Vim.

Performance

  • Fixed a multi-second freeze when opening a change with a very large diff (for example a Cargo.lock dependency bump). The diff gutter no longer repeats per-line work across the Rust bridge.
  • The diff cache is now keyed by commit id and keeps recently viewed changes warm, so jumping back to a change is instant and never shows a stale diff after an amend, rebase, or whitespace-mode toggle.

item.title: Version 0.2.23
item.description:
Conflict diffs

  • Conflicted files now render as first-class conflict blocks instead of raw jj marker text, with clearer section headers and compact provenance labels.
  • Side-by-side diff automatically falls back to unified rendering for conflicted files, so conflict blocks stay full-width and readable.

Conflict resolution

  • The SwiftUI conflict banner stays above the file diff and keeps the existing Use Ours / Use Theirs actions visible while reviewing the conflicted file.

Diff colors

  • Diff colors now come from a shared Rust theme and are reused by the SwiftUI diff renderer, keeping conflict, syntax, gutter, and search-highlight colors consistent.

Divergent changes

  • SwiftUI now renders divergent changes more reliably by resolving selected rows and detail views through the commit identity when a shared change ID is ambiguous.

item.title: Version 0.2.22
item.description:
Bookmark diffs

  • SwiftUI can now diff bookmark ranges from the DAG context menu and Bookmark Manager, showing the full change range from the fork point to the selected bookmark instead of only an interdiff between two revisions.
  • Bookmark revsets are quoted and displayed consistently, including names that need escaping, and compare direction keeps its title and labels when reversed.

Command palette jj commands

  • Run raw jj commands from the command palette with argument parsing, in-memory history, command output, and a copy-output action.
  • Successful raw commands refresh the repository view so quick status, log, diff, and operation-log checks can stay inside JayJay.

Find and revset fixes

  • Diff find now highlights visible matches immediately, distinguishes the current match, searches across side-by-side panes, and clears highlights when the native find bar closes.
  • Revset parsing now loads jj's default revset aliases through the CLI, so user config that references aliases such as builtin_immutable_heads() works in JayJay too. Fixes #60.

Internal

  • Split repository resolution into focused modules, model change authors with a shared CommitAuthor value, and removed obsolete agent config files from the codebase.

item.title: Version 0.2.21
item.description:
Word-wrap for diff views

  • Long lines in unified and side-by-side diffs now wrap to multiple visual rows instead of hiding the tail behind a horizontal scrollbar. Continuation rows share the same line number as their first row (blank gutter on the wraps) so the eye stays oriented.
  • Side-by-side wraps to the tallest side and pads the shorter pane with empty continuation rows, so the two panes — and their gutters — advance in lock-step. No more visual desync when one side has a long Removed line opposite a short Added line.

Short context runs stay inline

  • The context collapser used to fold any run of unchanged lines longer than the visible context. It now keeps runs of 2 lines or fewer inline — a one-line "N unmodified lines" separator was uglier than just showing them.
  • Separator label rewording: "N hidden lines" → "N unmodified lines" — they're not hidden, they're just unchanged.

Revert correctness

  • Revert Change (from the DAG context menu or command palette) now lands the reverse change as a child of the working copy, matching jj revert --onto @. Previously the reverse change was inserted between the target and its parent, which surprised users coming from the CLI and could pull unrelated commits along for the ride.

Internal

  • Split jj-diff's wrap module into a folder mod with focused submodules (cols.rs, chunks.rs, unified.rs, side_by_side.rs, ...); updated AGENTS.md to prefer folder modules over single long-file modules.
  • The macOS app's CLI-path resolver now uses a thread-safe getpwuid_r, filters relative PATH entries, checks the exec bit, and falls back to $SHELL if no login shell is available.

item.title: Version 0.2.20
item.description:
Hunk-level review

  • Mark individual change groups in the diff as reviewed — click the leftmost gutter pill on any line of a group to toggle. Pill is light blue (matching the right-click "Select Change Group" highlight) when unreviewed, solid accent with a white ✓ on the first line when reviewed. Working-copy diffs only.
  • Auto-promotes to file-marked when every change group in a file is reviewed; un-ticking one hunk on a file-marked file demotes only that hunk and keeps every other hunk's review state intact. The file row checkmark in the file column updates immediately.
  • New Hide reviewed files toggle (eye-slash icon) in the file column header — only appears when there are reviewed files to hide.
  • Tracked deletions can be marked reviewed too — identity is derived from the parent's bytes for the deleted file, so re-creating the file or rebasing onto a parent with different bytes invalidates the mark, while a rebase that keeps the same parent bytes preserves it.

Review state survives jj rebases

  • Review marks are now keyed to a per-file content identity computed in the Rust core from the diff's blob IDs. Rebases, amends, and squashes that produce identical bytes keep the marks; an edit to that file (or a rebase that changes the parent bytes for a deletion) invalidates only that file's marks. Marks on one path are no longer cleared by unrelated bytes elsewhere in the change. Old mtime-based entries are silently dropped on first launch.

Diff gutter polish

  • Removed the +/− marker column. The line backgrounds (red for removed, green for added) already convey the same information; the freed space goes to the new review pill.
  • When you right-click "Select Change Group", the system selection highlight now fully owns those rows — the review stripe steps out of the way until selection is dismissed.

GPUI shell (alpha)

  • File column rows widened so the path no longer clips when the filename + path together don't fit a tight row height.
  • Both filename and path now middle-truncate ("shell/mac/…/NativeDiffView.swift") based on the column width — same idea as SwiftUI's truncationMode(.middle). Resize the column wider to see more.
  • Side-by-side and unified diffs both drop the +/− marker column, matching the macOS shell.

Untracked remote bookmarks in the Bookmark Manager

  • Bookmarks that exist only as a remote ref — like feature@origin after jj git fetch when nobody's run jj bookmark track yet — now show up in the Bookmark Manager with a cloud-outline icon, a remote-only badge, and the @origin suffix rendered inline. Closes #55.
  • Right-click on a remote-only row gets you Filter in DAG (with the qualified name@remote so the revset resolves) and one Track name@remote action per available remote — handy for figuring out which collaborator's git branch a head in the DAG belongs to without dropping to the terminal.
  • The stats bar gains a N remote-only counter so you can see at a glance how many untracked branches you've fetched.

Internal

  • Extracted a shared jayjay_core::hash::hex_sha256 helper.
  • Removed old_marker / new_marker from SideBySideRow in the Rust core and uniffi bindings — no consumer left after the gutter rewrite.
  • DiffHunk now carries a canonical review_identity field computed in jayjay_core::repo::diff::entry::compute_review_identity from blob IDs. ReviewStore dropped its disk-hashing path entirely and is now a pure keyed store with caller-supplied identity — same shape Rust-side and Swift-side.
  • jayjay_core::Repo::list_bookmarks now also emits synthetic BookmarkInfo entries (with a new has_local_target: bool field) for remote bookmark names with no local target. Grouped per name; orphan refs are sorted by remote name for determinism.
  • Test suite stopped guarding every real_jj_repo test with redundant jj_is_available() / git_is_available() checks — CI installs both, and silently no-op'ing on missing binaries hid real failures.

item.title: Version 0.2.19
item.description:
Diff fixes

  • Selection clamps to end-of-line. Highlighting no longer trails into empty space past a line's last glyph, and multi-line selections that cross a short→long line transition now highlight every line in full instead of stopping at the previous line's width.

DAG polish

  • Lane connectors now draw short stubs through each node, so the graph reads as one continuous line through commits instead of breaking at every row.

Internal

  • Editor and terminal launch logic moved to jayjay-core (Rust) so the SwiftUI app and the in-progress GPUI shell share one implementation. No behavior change.

item.title: Version 0.2.18
item.description:
Diff polish

  • New Unified / Side-by-side toggle in the diff header — replaces the icon-only toggle so the active mode is unambiguous.

File list polish

  • Tree mode now supports folding directories: click a folder row's chevron to collapse, click again to expand. Fold state is per-window and survives change selection.
  • Hidden the always-on system scrollbar on the DAG and file lists (no behavior change beyond visual quiet).

Fixes

  • Fixed duplicate folder rows in the tree file list — directory entries now carry their full path so SwiftUI's ForEach can key them uniquely.
  • About window: Sponsor / Star on GitHub buttons no longer pick up the macOS default-button accent highlight on open.

Internal

  • DAG lane assignment moved to jayjay_core::dag (Rust). The Swift DAGLayout is now a thin uniffi wrapper, so the lane logic is shared with future shells.
  • jayjay-uniffi split into per-feature modules (dag, diff, error, repo, types); lib.rs is a thin umbrella.

item.title: Version 0.2.17
item.description:
Change evolution viewer

  • Right-click any mutable change in the DAG and pick Show evolution… to see every prior version of that change with operation labels (snapshot, describe, rebase, squash, split, new) and timestamps.
  • Click an entry to interdiff that version against the current head; click a file to see the side-by-side diff using the same engine as the rest of the app.
  • Right-click a row for Copy Commit ID or Copy ‘jj restore’ command — useful for recovering work after a botched rewrite.

Pull Request creation

  • Right-click a non-trunk bookmark (in the DAG row or Bookmark Manager) and pick Pull Request on GitHub to open the existing PR if there is one, or GitHub’s compose URL otherwise. Driven by the gh CLI when present.

Command palette

  • jj is now a first-class prefix alongside !. Type jj st, jj log, jj fix and so on to run the raw CLI with inline output.

Polish

  • Annotate, File History, and Evolution panels share a consistent Done button and esc keyboard shortcut for closing.
  • The Evolution list uses the standard pane background instead of a sidebar vibrancy material that looked off in light mode.
  • Annotate header now shows Annotate: <path> for symmetry with the History panel.

Internal

  • Evolog and file annotate now run in-process via jj_lib::evolution and jj_lib::annotate — no jj CLI shell-out, no template parsing.
  • File history switched to a type-safe revset (RevsetExpression::filter + FilesetExpression::file_path) instead of formatted strings.
  • New DetailPaneMode enum collapses five mutually-exclusive view-state booleans into a single value; annotate and history loaders now guard against stale completions hijacking the pane.

item.title: Version 0.2.16
item.description:
Diff editing

  • Added a grouped diff gutter for multi-line changes, with a dedicated group action column alongside deletion and addition line controls.
  • Change-group actions can now select or abandon a whole contiguous changed block without selecting lines one by one.
  • The group indicator uses a connected mild blue stripe and stays hidden for single-line changes.

Detail view

  • Made the change description area more compact so the diff is visible sooner.
  • Added a lightweight resize handle that previews height changes during drag and applies the layout change when released.

Internal

  • Split diff gutter actions into focused protocols for selection and edit behavior.
  • Cleaned up Clippy warnings in Rust core code.

item.title: Version 0.2.15
item.description:
Working copy fidelity

  • Auto-snapshots now respect Git's full ignore stack — local .gitignore, core.excludesFile, the default $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/git/ignore, and .git/info/exclude. Globally ignored files like .claude/ no longer appear as untracked changes in the working copy.
  • The macOS filesystem watcher now consults the same ignore matcher as the Rust core, so editing a globally-ignored file no longer triggers a stale "uncommitted changes" indicator.
  • Tracked files that match an ignore rule still surface change events, so edits to checked-in build artifacts continue to refresh the UI.

Commit box fix

  • The commit message now resets after a successful jj commit, so the new working copy starts with an empty draft instead of inheriting the previous message.
  • If a commit fails, the draft is preserved — previously the box was cleared optimistically and the message was lost.

Release tooling

  • just release now stops at the local artifact (zip + signed appcast); the new just shell::publish recipe creates the GitHub draft, uploads the zip, and bumps the Homebrew tap. gh release create uses --verify-tag, so publishing aborts cleanly if the v<version> tag has not been pushed.
  • Sparkle signing failures now fail the release outright instead of producing an unsigned appcast entry.

item.title: Version 0.2.13
item.description:
Diff view improvements

  • EOF-newline changes (a file that gains or loses its trailing newline) now render a visible ⊘↵ marker — matches GitHub Desktop. Previously they appeared as plain unchanged content.
  • When Ignore whitespace suppresses every line change, the diff pane now shows a banner instead of silently rendering an all-context view.
  • Files committed as Git LFS pointers no longer spin forever in the image preview when LFS is uninstalled — JayJay detects the pointer bytes and shows the placeholder text path.

DAG and commit box polish

  • Trunk-bookmarked commits (main / master / trunk) now render as diamonds; other bookmarked commits render as hollow accent-stroked circles — easier to scan the graph at a glance.
  • Commit-box drafts survive navigating away from @ and back. Previously the in-progress message was lost whenever another change was selected.
  • Bookmarks in the Detail header now have a copy button, matching the Change and Commit rows.

item.title: Version 0.2.12
item.description:
Drag-to-rebase in the DAG

  • Drag a change directly onto another change to run jj rebase without looking up change IDs
  • Hold-to-arm interaction reduces accidental drags and keeps single-click selection intact
  • Drag hover now shows a clear target outline, node ring, and inline rebase preview
  • Successful drag rebases show a toast with inline conflict follow-up and a one-click Undo action

DAG interaction polish

  • Clicking a change no longer recenters or scroll-jumps the DAG unexpectedly
  • The commit box is only shown for the working copy
  • The Dock menu now includes Open Repository… for faster access

Internal cleanup

  • Repo-level alerts, sheets, HUDs, and toasts now go through a consolidated presentation model
  • DAGRow and DAGView logic moved into focused view models to keep the UI code smaller and easier to test
  • Added macOS app tests for drag-rebase gesture policy and DAG row/view-model regressions, and wired them into CI via just test-app

item.title: Version 0.2.11
item.description:
Status bar + GitHub PR integration

  • New extensible status bar with four item types: plain text, clickable link, action, and picker
  • GitHub PR status via gh CLI — shows PR number, state (open/merged/closed), and checks icon (passing/failing/pending) for the selected change's bookmark
  • Click the PR status to open it in the browser; hover to see the PR title
  • Workspace picker migrated to the new model with nested menu support
  • gh CLI version shown in Settings alongside jj

Post-fetch cleanup for merged PRs

  • After Git Pull, changes that are empty after rebase AND whose remote tracking branch was deleted are auto-abandoned — the PR was already merged, no manual cleanup needed
  • Conflicting changes in the same situation get flagged in the toast message so you can decide

Enum types + serde structs

  • PrState (Open/Closed/Merged), ChecksStatus (Passing/Failing/Pending/None), GhCheckStatus, GhCheckConclusion — all serde-derived, no string comparisons in the parse path
  • JJStatus renamed to CliStatus — shared between jj and gh CLI checks
  • types.rs split into types/ module with 7 focused files

Other fixes

  • Toast dismiss time now scales with message length (2–8 seconds) so long messages are readable
  • Toast tap-to-dismiss works on the full background area, not just the text
  • CI dedup: push trigger restricted to main — PRs no longer run duplicate checks
  • Docs: Myers → Histogram diff algorithm references corrected across README and landing page
  • Fixed broken Roadmap.md link in CONTRIBUTING.md

item.title: Version 0.2.10
item.description:
Diff view fixes

  • Long lines no longer wrap in the unified diff — each diff line is exactly one row so the gutter and content stay aligned. Long lines scroll horizontally instead
  • Row backgrounds (red/green) now fill cleanly edge-to-edge under the no-wrap layout
  • Abandon Selected Lines on the working copy refreshes the diff pane correctly

Rename detection

  • Batch moves (multiple files from one directory to another) are now paired correctly by filename instead of cascade-misassigning on the file list
  • Empty content no longer scores as "identical" — an unrelated deletion in a batch can't steal a rename slot

Working copy auto-refresh

  • Reviewing the working copy + external file save → refresh button shows the pending indicator instead of yanking your selection and scroll mid-review
  • Reviewing another change + working copy change → graph silently updates so the WC entry stays current
  • User actions (Abandon Selected Lines, Describe, Split, …) refresh immediately without a ghost "files changed" flash from the FS echo

Other fixes

  • Repos with many files no longer stuck at loading — fixed a pipe deadlock in the LFS path probe where git's stdout filled up while we were still writing to its stdin
  • Welcome view centers the logo when there are no recent repos; repo list is scrollable when long

Internal

  • Diff rendering extracted into a JayJayDiffUI Swift package — cleaner separation between app glue (DiffSection, DiffStore) and reusable rendering primitives
  • New test target on JayJayDiffUI with regression tests for the no-wrap alignment, background fill width, and rename batching

item.title: Version 0.2.9
item.description:
Image diff rendering

  • PNG, JPG, GIF, WebP, HEIC, BMP, TIFF, ICO, ICNS now render as actual images instead of <binary file> text
  • Side-by-side before/after for modified files; single pane for added, removed, and renamed
  • Pixel dimensions and file size shown under each pane
  • 32×32 icons render at 1:1 — no upscale-blur
  • Checkerboard background for transparent regions

SVG rich-view toggle

  • SVG files keep the text diff by default
  • Eye-icon toggle in the diff header switches to a rendered WKWebView view

DAG + file list keyboard navigation

  • j / ↓ / Ctrl-n → next change
  • k / ↑ / Ctrl-p → previous change
  • Same bindings work in the file list when it's the active pane
  • DAG receives focus on cold launch and new repo windows — no clicking required
  • Multi-window safe — only the key window's DAG responds to keys

Other fixes

  • Settings → Open jj config now respects the configured editor
  • jj fix config uses absolute paths so formatters work regardless of shell
  • Histogram diff algorithm (via similar 3.0) — matches jj diff and reads better on code than Myers

Internal

  • New extensible DiffPreview enum on DiffHunk — adding PDF/video preview is now a single enum variant
  • Test coverage for the image preview pipeline
  • update-appcast.py now prepends new entries instead of clobbering the entire file

item.title: Version 0.2.8
item.description:
What's New

  • Myers diff algorithm — via similar crate, same as GitHub Desktop
  • Divergent commit support — badge, commitId-based actions, resolve option
  • Bookmark Manager — Cmd+Shift+B, stats, filter, clean up, resolve conflicts
  • Commit avatars — GitHub + Gravatar for any email
  • Scrollable descriptions — see full PR messages and Co-authored-by
  • jj-lib 0.40 + tree-sitter 0.26.8

Performance

  • Cargo.lock diff: 15s → instant (Myers O(n*d) vs O(n²) LCS)
  • Preload all file diffs on change selection

Bug Fixes

  • Fixed jj new/jj edit "descendants not rebased" — proper snapshot + rebase lifecycle
  • Fixed multi-window Repository menu dispatching to wrong window
  • Fixed DAG scroll recycling with divergent commits (ForEach identity)

item.title: Version 0.2.7
item.description:
• DiffStore — extracted diff caching and preloading
  • DiffEdit context collapsing — shared Rust implementation
  • Menu icons — SF Symbols on all menus
  • Protocol-based menu system — reliable in all window types
  • Toast HUD dismisses on click

item.title: Version 0.2.6
item.description:

  • Rebase selected onto context menu action
  • O(n) diff — prefix/suffix trimming for large files
  • Fixed jj edit crash and config check false alarm
